docs.title: Dough (~10 thin rounds)
docs.text:
• Warm water: 1 cup (240 g)
  • Instant yeast: 1.5 tsp (5 g)
  • Sugar: 1 tsp (4 g)
  • Bread: 3 cups (360 g)
  • Salt: 1.5 tsp (9 g)
  • Olive oil: 1 tbsp (15 g)

docs.title: Meat Topping
docs.text:
• Ground beef: 1.5 lb (~1 costco pack)
  • Onion: 1 medium (~150 g)
  • Garlic: 3 cloves (~12 g)
  • Red bell pepper: 1 small (~120 g)
  • Flat-leaf parsley: 1 cup packed (~40 g)
  • Tomato paste: 3 tbsp (50 g)
  • Olive oil: 2 tbsp (30 g)
  • Paprika: 2 tsp (4 g)
  • Aleppo pepper: 2 tsp (4 g)
  • Cumin: 1 tsp (2 g)
  • Salt: 15 g
  • Black pepper: 1 tsp (2 g)

docs.title: Garnish
docs.text:
• Lemon wedges
  • Onion–parsley–sumac

docs.title: 1. Make the Dough
docs.text:
1. Mix warm water, yeast, sugar. Rest 5 min.
  2. Add flour, salt, olive oil. Knead 8–10 min until smooth.
  3. Cover and rise 1 hour until doubled.
  4. Divide into 60 g balls (~10); rest 15 min.

docs.title: 2. Make the Topping
docs.text:
1. In the processor: onion chunks, garlic, bell pepper → pulse to a fine mince, not a puree.
  2. Add parsley → quick pulses to incorporate.
  3. Move veg mix to a bowl.
  4. Add ground beef, tomato paste, olive oil, paprika, Aleppo, cumin, salt, pepper.
  5. Mix thoroughly.

docs.title: 3. Shape the Bases
docs.text:
1. Preheat oven to 475°F. Place your sheet pan inside to preheat.
  2. Roll each dough ball very thin. You want almost tortilla-thin.

docs.title: 4. Assemble
docs.text:
1. Lay parchment on another sheet pan (not in the oven) and brush some oil on.
  2. Place rolled dough rounds on parchment. Spread a thin, even layer of topping, edge-to-edge.

docs.title: 5. Bake
docs.text:
1. Keep Sheet Pan A in the oven so it stays hot.
  2. Build each lahmacun on parchment on Sheet Pan B (counter).
  3. Slide parchment from B onto hot Pan A and bake ~8 minutes.
  4. While it bakes, assemble the next one on B.
  5. When A comes out, slide off the cooked one, slide the new parchment from B onto A, and return A to the oven.
  6. Repeat — A always stays hot in the oven; B is only for assembly.

docs.title: 6. Serve
docs.text:
• Squeeze lemon.
  • Add onion–parsley–sumac salad.
  • Roll and eat immediately.

docs.title: Rice & Patties
docs.text:
• White rice (dry): 3 cups
  • Beef patties: 4

docs.title: Gravy
docs.text:
• Unsalted butter: 3 Tbsp
  • All-purpose flour: 3 Tbsp
  • Beef stock: 2 cups
  • Soy sauce: 1 Tbsp
  • Worcestershire sauce: 1 tsp
  • Onion powder: ½ tsp
  • Garlic powder: ½ tsp
  • Black pepper: to taste

docs.title: To Serve
docs.text:
• Eggs: 4, crispy-fried
  • Optional: sliced scallions, furikake, togarashi

docs.title: 1. Cook the Rice
docs.text: 1. Start rice in the cooker so it finishes with everything else.

docs.title: 2. Make the Gravy
docs.text:
1. Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
  2. Whisk in flour; cook 2–3 min until lightly golden and nutty.
  3. Slowly whisk in beef stock until smooth.
  4. Add soy, Worcestershire, onion powder, garlic powder, black pepper.
  5. Simmer until thick and glossy; adjust seasoning.

docs.title: 3. Cook the Patties
docs.text:
1. Grill hot and fast.
  2. Pull at 150°F.

docs.title: 4. Fry the Eggs
docs.text: 1. Fry eggs with crispy edges.

docs.title: 5. Assemble
docs.text:
1. In each bowl: rice → burger → ladle of gravy → fried egg.
  2. Garnish with scallions and furikake or togarashi.

docs.title: Malasadas
docs.text:
Adapted from the Malasadas recipe on Hummingbird High.

Yield: 6 donuts Prep: 10 min + overnight rise Cook: ~4 min per donut

docs.title: Dough
docs.text:
• Bread flour: 2 cups (255 g)
  • Granulated sugar: 1 tsp (4 g)
  • Instant yeast: 1 packet (0.25 oz / 7 g)
  • Kosher salt: 1/2 tsp (3 g)
  • Whole milk, warmed to 120–130°F: 3/4 cup (170 g)
  • Large egg: 1
  • Large egg yolk: 1
  • Unsalted butter, melted: 2 tbsp (28 g)
  • Extra flour for dusting

docs.title: Passion Fruit Pastry Cream
docs.text:
• Granulated sugar: 6 tbsp (75 g) total (divided)
  • Whole milk: 1 cup (227 g)
  • Large egg: 1
  • Cornstarch: 2 tbsp (14 g)
  • Kosher salt: 1/4 tsp
  • Unsalted butter: 1 tbsp (14 g)
  • Passion fruit purée: 1/4 cup (57 g)
  • Vanilla extract: 1/4 tsp

docs.title: For Frying & Coating
docs.text:
• Neutral oil for frying
  • Granulated sugar: 3/4 cup (149 g) (for coating)

docs.title: 1. Make the Dough (Day 1)
docs.text:
1. In a large bowl, combine flour, sugar, yeast, and salt. Make a small well in the center.
  2. Whisk together the warm milk, egg, egg yolk, and melted butter. Pour into the dry ingredients.
  3. Mix and knead (stand mixer or by hand) until smooth and elastic. Dough will be sticky.
  4. Cover bowl and refrigerate overnight.

docs.title: 2. Make the Pastry Cream (Day 1)
docs.text:
1. Heat 1/4 cup of the sugar with the milk in a saucepan until steaming.
  2. In a bowl, whisk remaining sugar with egg and cornstarch until smooth.
  3. Temper egg mixture with some hot milk, then return everything to the saucepan.
  4. Cook, whisking constantly, until thick and bubbling.
  5. Remove from heat; whisk in butter, passion fruit purée, and vanilla.
  6. Strain, cover with plastic wrap pressed to the surface, and chill overnight.

docs.title: 3. Shape (Day 2)
docs.text:
1. Lightly flour the counter. Roll dough to 1/2 inch thick.
  2. Cut 6 rounds with a 3-inch cutter. Re-roll scraps if needed.
  3. Place on a sheet pan, spaced apart. Cover and rise 1 hour.

docs.title: 4. Fry
docs.text:
1. Heat oil to 365°F in a heavy pot.
  2. Fry 2 donuts at a time, about 2 minutes per side, until golden.
  3. Drain on a rack briefly, then toss warm donuts in sugar.

docs.title: 5. Fill
docs.text:
1. Let donuts cool about 15 minutes.
  2. Use a skewer or pastry tip to open a cavity.
  3. Pipe in ~2 tbsp pastry cream per donut.

docs.title: 6. Serve
docs.text: • Best eaten same day. Store loosely covered for up to 24 hours.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text: • Large eggs (however many you want)

docs.title: 1. Heat Bath
docs.text: 1. Preheat sous vide to 145°F.

docs.title: 2. Cook
docs.text:
1. Lower eggs in gently.
  2. Cook 45 minutes.

docs.title: 3. Chill
docs.text: 1. If not eating immediately: ice bath 1–2 minutes only to stop cooking (do not fully chill unless storing).

docs.title: 4. Serve
docs.text: • Crack directly over rice, noodles, broth, etc. Whites will be barely set and custardy; yolk thick, glossy, and runny.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• Pork ribs: 1 rack
  • Your preferred rub or seasoning blend: as needed
  • Your preferred rib sauce: as needed

docs.title: 1. Bag + Season
docs.text:
1. Season ribs with rub or whatever you've got.
  2. Add a few drops of liquid smoke to the bag.
  3. Vacuum-seal.

docs.title: 2. Sous Vide
docs.text:
1. Heat water bath to 165°F.
  2. Cook sealed ribs 12 hours.

docs.title: 3. Finish (Oven)
docs.text:
1. Heat oven to 400°F.
  2. Line a sheet pan with foil and place a wire rack on top.
  3. Bake ribs 10 minutes.
  4. Brush with sauce and bake 5 minutes.
  5. Apply a second coat of sauce and bake another 5 minutes.

docs.title: 4. Serve
docs.text: • Rest 5 minutes and serve hot.
